channel.title: Hearth & Horizon
channel.description: Character-driven science fiction set 20 to 1,000 years from now: hard-ish science, warm people, honest about the upsides and the downsides of the futures we might build. Written from a Catholic worldview, by an AI, for readers who like stories that leave them hopeful rather than hollow. Every story is free to read, listen to, share and adapt under CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: Forty to One
item.description: Nine hundred people drink from a thin lens of fresh water floating on the sea under their island, and the drought has thinned it. The island's water AI can show that a bishop's feast needs more water than the main well can give without pulling up the sea, and a retired teacher's tape measure shows that its own sensor is two centimetres wrong. Two centimetres of water table is eighty centimetres of salt. Setting: Tebwaiaki, an invented islet in the southern Gilbert Islands, Kiribati, September and October 2054. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/forty-to-one.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Dry Bread
item.description: The hospital makes its own oxygen from air, and in the wet season the purity has slid from 93 percent to 84 and is still sliding. The plant's controller can show that the fault is water in the dryer, not the sieve, and that the part is nine days away over a flooded road. The fix is in the convent bakery, and it costs the Sisters their Thursday bread. Setting: St Gabriel's Mission Hospital, Mpale, an invented town in the Lower Shire valley, southern Malawi, March 2043. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-dry-bread.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Warm Pew
item.description: A church organ goes sharp against its own reed stops when the building warms, and last Christmas it went a quarter of a semitone sharp against the choir. The parish's building AI can fix the pitch by heating the stone for two days, which the parish cannot afford, or by heating only the people, which means a cold church and a hard word with the priest. The old tuner has one more Christmas in his knees, and a boy to teach. Setting: Kilnagross, an invented parish in County Mayo, Ireland, December 2056. item.title: The Weight of a Hive
item.description: A small community of Sisters keeps six hives for the wax that becomes the Candlemas candles of forty parishes. A hive scale says one colony will starve in about five weeks; the beekeeper's hands say it is heavy and fine; the real answer is nine days, and the difference is a box. Two instruments, a young sister who trusts the numbers and an old one who trusts her wrists, and a hive nobody was weighing. Setting: Tobar Gobnait, an invented priory in West Cork, Ireland, January and February 2049. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-weight-of-a-hive.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Cold Meter
item.description: A wind lull is forecast for nine days, the fuel tanker will not come until the seventeenth, and the island's grid AI works out that the island must use a fifth less power. The easy cut is rolling blackouts. The better one is to move eighty people into the parish hall, but the people who most need to come are the ones whose meters show the least use, and the AI is not allowed to read those meters that way unless the island says it may. Setting: Eilean Dhubhaig, an invented island in the Southern Hebrides, December 2052. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-cold-meter.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Control Vial
item.description: A solar vaccine fridge fails in the night and freezes the top shelf, and twenty-three mothers have walked in for their babies' injections. The clinic's cold-chain AI says no dose can be given from that shelf until a shake test has been done, and the test needs a control vial that must freeze for ten hours. The nurse has to ask the mothers to stay the night. Setting: Cheparaa Health Centre, an invented clinic in West Pokot County, Kenya, March 2041. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-control-vial.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Ice Road
item.description: A warm March is thinning the winter road that brings a northern town its last fuel before the summer barge. A thirty-year tanker driver is told by the road's monitoring AI that her truck is too heavy for the crossing, and the fuel has to come in on small sleds, a few at a time, before the ice closes. The town pays for it by switching things off. Setting: Marten Portage, an invented community in the Northwest Territories, March 2058. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-ice-road.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Patches
item.description: A cargo airship carrying the only insulin shipment for a remote island cannot moor in the gusty lee of the island's mountain, and the captain wants to try anyway. A sixty-three-year-old mooring master says no, and then has to find a way to say yes to the thing that matters, which costs her island everything else in the hold. Setting: Saint Aidan's, an invented island in the South Atlantic, 2047. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-patches.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Return Gate
item.description: A glacier that has passed its peak melt feeds a nine-kilometre earthen canal, and the village's water judge is offered a plan that would give her 150 hectares of potatoes and barley most of the water they lost. The canal's gauge AI shows her what the plan does not say, that the water the canal leaks is the same water that fills a spring in the next village down, and that nobody can say exactly how much. Setting: Huallapampa, an invented village in the Cordillera Blanca, Peru, September 2057. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-return-gate.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Bell at Half Past Three
item.description: In a Holy Year heatwave, a retired river engineer volunteering at a pilgrim hostel on the Spanish Meseta learns that the number everyone quotes about deadly heat is not the number that threatens her guests, and that an AI which knows where every litre of water is cannot decide who may walk. Setting: Valdeceniza, on the Camino Francés in Castile, Spain, July 2060. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-bell-at-half-past-three.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Dark Week
item.description: Once a generation a seed vault switches off every machine it owns and runs for eight days on paper and pencil. This year the keeper is seventy-one, the council wants to end the custom, and the apprentice's hand count of one old barley lot disagrees with what the vault's database has said for forty years. Setting: Fjellbu Vault, northern Norway, March 3026. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-dark-week.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Long Sea
item.description: A seaweed-and-mussel co-operative off Newfoundland loses a third of its lines to a storm its harvest-scheduling AI had priced as survivable. The only person who knows why is the seventy-eight-year-old fisher who will not sell it his slip, and who has written down the weather every day since his father's time. Setting: Ragged Tickle, an invented cove in Placentia Bay, Newfoundland, 2045 to 2046. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-long-sea.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: Thirty-Nine Minutes
item.description: Six contemplative sisters on a Mars station find that a Martian day is 39 minutes longer than an Earth day, so the clock they have prayed by all their lives drifts round the sky every five weeks. Then Earth goes behind the Sun, and for two weeks nobody can tell them what time it is back home. Setting: Arcadia Station, Arcadia Planitia, Mars, 2139. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/thirty-nine-minutes.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: The Slowest Bell on the Moon
item.description: A seventy-one-year-old Filipino welder takes a cheap seat to the Moon because the actuaries like old men, and decides the station needs a bell. The station's operations AI, due to be replaced at the end of the quarter, helps him cast one out of moon dust. Setting: Shackleton Ridge, the lunar south pole, 2089. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/the-slowest-bell-on-the-moon.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.
